_readme: Curated legal-name to brand aliases for organization-to-endpoint resolution.
String matching gets a long way and then stops dead. The directory records
legal entities and the EHR vendors publish brands, and for the largest
health systems the two share no tokens at all: 'UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH
PHYSICIANS' is UPMC's physician group and the strings have nothing in
common. No normalization rule recovers that, and every attempt to loosen
one produced a false merge instead (see the Penn Medicine / Penn State
Health case in h53_org_endpoint_resolution.py).
So the remaining links are curated rather than inferred. Each entry names
one publicly verifiable corporate fact and carries the source that states
it. That is auditable in a way a similarity threshold is not: a reader can
disagree with a specific row and check it, and a wrong row is a wrong
claim about one organization rather than a silent systematic error.
Rules for adding an entry:
- `ndh_name` must be the exact normalized NDH organization name.
- `brand` must match an organization name a vendor actually publishes.
- `basis` must be checkable by a reader without insider knowledge.
- If the relationship is uncertain, leave it out. Coverage is not worth
a wrong endpoint: sending a patient's app to the wrong health system
is a worse outcome than telling them we do not know.
Aliased links are reported as their own tier and never counted as
deterministic.
The brand must be the label as the cached vendor file publishes it today.
h53_org_endpoint_resolution.check_aliases raises when an alias matches no
vendor label in its state, because a renamed brand otherwise resolves
nothing and reports no error. On 2026-10-16 (FHI-73) nine of thirteen PA
aliases were dead that way: Epic publishes 'MyUPMC', 'TempleHealth' and
'Thomas Jefferson University Health System', and no cached vendor file
publishes a 'Penn State Health' brand in PA. The two Penn State Health
aliases were removed rather than repointed: Oracle Health lists 'Penn State
Health Care Partners' (Reading, PA) with NPIs that the NDH files under other
organizations' names too (a Tower Health Medical Group anesthesia entity,
Haven Behavioral Hospital), so an alias to it would be a guess. Those NPIs
reach the endpoint through the NPI tier instead, which states what it is.

aliases.basis: University of Pittsburgh Physicians is UPMC's employed physician group; UPMC publishes it as part of the UPMC system on upmc.com and it shares UPMC's Epic tenancy. Epic publishes UPMC's patient-access brand as 'MyUPMC' (epicent-prd-rp.upmc.com).
Named UPMC in its own legal business name. Epic publishes UPMC's patient-access brand as 'MyUPMC' (epicent-prd-rp.upmc.com).
The University of Pennsylvania Health System trades as Penn Medicine.

aliases.ndh_name: CLINICAL PRACTICES OF THE UNIVERSITY OF PENNSYLVANIA
aliases.basis: Clinical Practices of the University of Pennsylvania is the faculty practice plan of Penn Medicine.

Lancaster General Health joined the University of Pennsylvania Health System in 2015 and trades as Penn Medicine Lancaster General Health. Epic publishes Lancaster General Health as its own brand, 'Lancaster', with its own endpoint (epicproxy.lghealth.org) and LG Health care sites beneath it; the earlier alias to 'Penn Medicine' pointed these practitioners at the University of Pennsylvania tenant instead.
Allegheny Clinic is the employed physician organization of Allegheny Health Network.

Jefferson University Physicians is the faculty practice of Thomas Jefferson University, which operates Jefferson Health. Epic publishes the brand as 'Thomas Jefferson University Health System' (fhir.jefferson.edu).
Temple Faculty Practice Plan is the physician organization of Temple University Health System, which trades as Temple Health. Epic publishes the brand as 'TempleHealth' (epicaccess.templehealth.org).
Temple Physicians Inc is a subsidiary of Temple University Health System. Epic publishes the brand as 'TempleHealth' (epicaccess.templehealth.org).
PinnacleHealth was acquired by UPMC in 2017 and operates as UPMC in Central Pa. Epic lists PinnacleHealth care sites (for example 'PinnacleHealth FamilyCare Middletown') under its 'MyUPMC' brand.
Bradford Regional and Elk Regional joined UPMC as UPMC Cole and UPMC Bradford. Epic lists 'UPMC Cole', 'UPMC Kane' and 'UPMC Outpatient Center - Bradford' under its 'MyUPMC' brand.
